record.paper_title: Selected Open Problems in Continuous-Time Quantum Walks
record.context_brief: Perfect state transfer edge-vs-diameter lower bounds
record.original_question: Let G be a graph with adjacency matrix A and transition matrix U(t)=exp(itA). Suppose G admits perfect state transfer between two vertices, meaning that for some time t and some unit-modulus complex number γ one has U(t)e_u = γ e_v. If G has m edges and diameter D, prove an asymptotic lower bound on m that is stronger than the currently known cubic bound by showing that m belongs to Ω(D^k) for some exponent k>3.

evidence.quote: Formally, perfect state transfer occurs at a G between vertices u and v at time t if there is a complex number γ of absolute value 1 so that U(t)e_u = γ e_v.
If perfect state transfer occurs in a graph with m edges of diameter D, show that m in Ω(D^k), for k>3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph with adjacency matrix $A$, and define the continuous-time quantum walk transition matrix $U(t) = \exp(itA)$ for $t \in \mathbb{R}$. For distinct vertices $u,v \in V$, denote by $e_u, e_v$ the standard basis vectors of $\mathbb{C}^V$. We say that $G$ admits perfect state transfer between $u$ and $v$ if there exist a time $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and a complex number $\gamma$ with $|\gamma|=1$ such that
$$U(t)\, e_u = \gamma\, e_v.$$
Let $m = |E|$ denote the number of edges of $G$ and let $D$ denote the diameter of $G$. It is known that whenever a graph admits perfect state transfer between some pair of vertices at distance $D$, one has $m \in \Omega(D^3)$. 

Establish a stronger asymptotic lower bound: prove that there exists an exponent $k > 3$ such that, for every infinite family of graphs admitting perfect state transfer between vertices at diameter $D$, one has $m \in \Omega(D^k)$.
artifact.category_tag: continuous-time quantum walks / perfect state transfer
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on continuous-time quantum walks (e.g., 2025 work on peak state transfer) still treats the cubic bound m = Ω(D^3) as the best known lower bound for perfect state transfer, with constructions achieving cubic edge count for the relaxed peak state transfer notion. No improvement to an exponent k>3 for perfect state transfer has been reported, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Peak state transfer in continuous quantum walks
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of graphs achieving peak state transfer at distance D have number of edges cubic in D; perfect state transfer at arbitrary distances is not known with polynomial growth.
status_evidence.claim: The cubic bound remains the relevant scale; no super-cubic lower bound for perfect state transfer is established.
